chunks: Ja'far ibn Ali al-Kufi narrated to me from his grandfather al-Hasan ibn Ali ibn Abdullah ibn al-Mughira, from al-Sakuni, from Ja'far ibn Muhammad, from his father, from his forefathers, from the Commander of the Faithful (peace be upon him), who said:
The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'Blessed is he who leaves a present lust for a promised [reward] he has not seen.'

key_terms.شَهْوَةً حَاضِرَةً: A present/immediate lust or desire, referring to tangible worldly temptations
key_terms.طُوبَى: Blessedness or glad tidings, a specific term of congratulation for Paradise
key_terms.لِمَوْعُودٍ: For a promised [reward], referring to the unseen rewards of the Hereafter

ai.seo_question: What is the reward for avoiding worldly lust for the sake of the unseen hereafter?
ai.summary: Recorded in Shaykh al-Saduq’s *Thawab al-A’mal* via the chain of the Ahl al-Bayt, this hadith emphasizes the spiritual merit of *zuhd* (asceticism) by linking the suppression of present lust to the assurance of unseen divine rewards. It underscores the Shia ethical principle that temporal sacrifice is an investment in the eternal, reflecting the Prophetic tradition of prioritizing the Hereafter over worldly impulses.

en.sayed-athar-husain-rizvi-&-sayed-maqs: 1.  Imam Ja’far Sadiq (a.s.) narrates from his predecessors that the Holy Prophet (s.a.w.s.) said, “Tooba (Congratulations) be for one who avoids lust today for the sake of those promised things he has not seen.”
